entries.name: control-honest-if-accept#0
entries.script: { (if (false) 1 else 2) == 2 }  // JVM: the control — both branches are Int, so nothing lies and the If shape itself evaluates. Green everywhere; a red here means the implementation refuses a mismatched-branch If at PARSE, which would make the twelve rejects below green for the wrong reason

entries.name: valdef-errored#1
entries.script: { val x = (if (false) 1 else 2L); true }  // JVM: BlockValue checks each ValDef's value (values.scala:1027) — Value.checkType -> SType.isValueOfType compares the value against the node's STATIC type; the Long that `if (false) 1 else 2L` returns is not an Int. The diagnostic names the ValDef node itself, which is what distinguishes this site from the result check below

entries.name: block-result-errored#2
entries.script: { { val y = 1; (if (false) 1 else 2L) } == 2 }  // JVM: BlockValue checks its RESULT (values.scala:1034) — Value.checkType -> SType.isValueOfType compares the value against the node's STATIC type; the Long that `if (false) 1 else 2L` returns is not an Int. The well-typed ValDef keeps the :1027 check from firing first

entries.name: if-branch-errored#6

The outer If takes its true branch, which is the inner If, whose own declared type is Int

entries.script: { Coll(if (false) 1 else 2L).size == 1 }  // JVM: ConcreteCollection checks each item (values.scala:894) — Value.checkType -> SType.isValueOfType compares the value against the node's STATIC type; the Long that `if (false) 1 else 2L` returns is not an Int. The check runs BEFORE the item is stored into the typed array, so this is a type error and not an ArrayStoreException

entries.name: fold-zero-errored#12
entries.script: { Coll[Int]().fold(if (false) 1 else 2L, { (p: (Int, Int)) => p._1 }) == 2 }  // JVM: Fold checks its ZERO (transformers.scala:227) — Value.checkType -> SType.isValueOfType compares the value against the node's STATIC type; the Long that `if (false) 1 else 2L` returns is not an Int.
